name: Question 6
problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
{\begin{aligned}z+x=2 \\ 2y-3z=1 \\ 2z-y=-3x+3\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+z=2 \\ 2y-3z=1 \\ 3x-y+2z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4-3)-0+(0-6) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 9 & -6 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -9 & -6 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -9 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -9 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -9 & -1 & 3 \\ -6 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=1,y=2,z=1.$

Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix: {z+x=22y−3z=12z−y=−3x+3

a
x=1,y=−2,z=−1
b
x=2,y=1,z=1
c
x=−1,y=−1,z=2
d
x=1,y=1,z=2
e
x=1,y=2,z=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first: {x+z=22y−3z=13x−y+2z=3

We wish to write this system in the form Ax=b, where A is a 3×3 matrix and x and b are 3×1 column vectors. We can do this as follows: [10102−33−12][xyz]=[213].

Now, the solution to Ax=b is given by x=A−1b. So, we compute A−1 as follows:

Step 1:

det(A)=|10102−33−12|=1|2−3−12|−0|0−332|+1|023−1|=(4−3)−0+(0−6)=−5.

Step 2:

M=[|2−3−12||0−332||023−1||01−12||1132||103−1||012−3||110−3||1002|]=[19−61−1−1−2−32].

Step 3:

C=[1−9−6−1−11−232].

Step 4:

CT=[1−1−2−9−13−612].

Step 5:

A−1=1det(A)CT=−15[1−1−2−9−13−612].

Hence x=A−1b=−15[1−1−2−9−13−612][213]=[121]. Hence the solution is x=1,y=2,z=1.
